items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Stefen Garcia, a Zeno captain, 36 years old.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: For unknown reasons—likely connected to Manus Vindictae—he moved into this motel.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: He attempted to make contact with Zeno several times, all of which failed.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: During his stay, he was tortured by increasingly intense hallucinations, delusion, and fear.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: And as a result ...

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: As a result, he committed suicide.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: And that's everything the evidence shows.
Chaotic clues are rolling in the mind, like a churning stomach.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: No.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: We must've overlooked something.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: A military officer killing himself; a phone call asking for help in Morse code.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Not to mention Manus Vindictae.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Where's this going, boss?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: We've encountered a series of bizarre events, one after another, ever since we arrived at this motel.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: The rituals in the rooms, the officer that went mad, the spirit in the mirror, and Manus Vindictae.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Only one person remains uninvolved.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Are you tryna say that she's the mastermind behind all this?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: She should know more about all this than anyone, yet she feigns ignorance at every turn, which is suspicious in its own right.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: But what's there for a motel housekeeper to gain from all this? It's not like these spooky scandals would attract more guests.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Unless someone else is pulling the strings, but that don't make much sense either, does it?

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: When all these unusual things happened, she was happy to stand by and watch, but by whose orders? Some larger, more mysterious organization?

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Gimme a break.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: What if she doesn't desire money or power?

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: So what you're saying is that you need to ask Little Miss Maid a couple more questions.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Precisely.
Argus sighs.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: That spirit morphed into Kayla, so it must've seen her face at some point. Which means that, at one time, Kayla was in this room.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: And you're right. Tuesday's definitely not a run-of-the-mill motel maid. It wouldn't be wise to approach her rashly.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Let me finish up here first, then we can go question her together.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Alright.
After a moment, Argus shakes her head in disappointment.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Nope. I got nothing.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Let's go find that maid. I have a few questions for her myself.
She makes her way across the room and opens the door. She freezes.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Where'd the body go?
The corpse that had been lying in the hallway has vanished, leaving only a pool of blood on the floor.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Ain't no signs of dragging, neither. Who, and how?

items.speaker: Telephone
items.text: *ring-ring-ring—*
The ringing echoes through the doorway.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: The phone again.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: What do you think? Should we answer it? I bet it's another one of those prank calls.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Those weren't prank calls. Someone was sending a distress signal in Morse code.
She picks up the receiver and presses the speaker button.
Could you tell me what year it is now?
A soft voice plays through the speaker.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Who's this?
This is Barbara.
